text:
maria: hey team — customer on private VPC seeing short bursts where the sidecar returns 429 and their k8s ingress also reports connection resets. customer says the bursts are traffic spikes from an internal job that fires every minute. asking for quick hedging / smoothing advice and safe config to avoid billing surprises.

customer-ops: repro summary: spike ~300-1200 req/s for ~10-30s, p95 latency up, many 429s from local sidecar limiter. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:09Z sidecar rate_limiter: allow=false tenant=acme remaining=0 refill_ms=1000
2026-03-15T14:02:09Z ingress error: upstream returned 429
```
headers: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, client ip shows multiple internal ips behind NAT.

sam: key Qs: what algorithm is the sidecar using (token bucket / leaky bucket)? are limits per-client-ip or per-tenant? if they're behind NAT you'll want per-tenant rather than per-ip. also check whether ingress preserves `x-request-id` or `x-idempotency-key` for dedupe.

jonathan: some concrete options (short list):
1) smoothing at sidecar level: switch to token-bucket with a larger `burst` and a moderate `refill` so short spikes are absorbed.
2) local short queue + shed oldest when full (bounded queue) so p99 latencies don't explode.
3) hedging at router: duplicate a request to a warm standby replica after X ms (only for idempotent ops). only do this if you can dedupe on backend or accept duplicate billing.

example Envoy local rate limit filter for token-bucket style smoothing:
```yaml
filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
    stat_prefix: sidecar_local_rl
    token_bucket:
      max_tokens: 200    # burst tokens
      tokens_per_fill: 50
      fill_interval: 1s
```

maria: they're using the open-source sidecar (go-based) with token bucket per-tenant currently set to max_tokens=50 tokens_per_fill=10 fill=1s. so clearly too small to absorb 10s spikes. ingress is nginx in front of the sidecar.

lee: nginx specifics — bump `limit_conn`/`limit_req` burst settings carefully. if using `limit_req` use `burst` + `nodelay` or without `nodelay` depending on whether you want smoothing vs immediate rejects. also increase `proxy_read_timeout` and enable `proxy_buffers` so backend stalls don't cascade. sample snippet: 
```nginx
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=one:10m rate=100r/s;
server {
  location / {
    limit_req zone=one burst=200;
    proxy_buffering on;
    proxy_buffers 8 16k;
  }
}
```

customer-ops: any precautions for billing? hedging duplicates will look like two requests hitting our billing meter.

maria: yes — hedged duplicates count as two inbound requests at the platform edge by default. recommend adding a dedupe key header `x-idempotency-key` set by client. on our side we can also honor `x-request-id` for dedupe within a short window to avoid double-charging for retries. document this with the customer before enabling hedging. :white_check_mark:

sam: quick mitigation plan I recommend we run immediately: 
- bump sidecar token_bucket to `max_tokens=300 tokens_per_fill=100 fill_interval=1s` (temporary)
- enable a small local queue size 200 requests, FIFO with tail-drop
- configure nginx `limit_req` burst=250 for the ingress layer
- add `Retry-After` header when returning 429 so clients back off
- schedule follow-up to tune to real traffic; collect p50/p95/p99 and burst histograms

commands (apply patch):
```bash
kubectl -n acme patch configmap sidecar-ratelimit --patch '\n{"data":{"token_bucket.max_tokens":"300","token_bucket.tokens_per_fill":"100"}}'\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/acme-sidecar
```

jonathan: long-term suggestions: use per-tenant meters (not per-source-ip), instrument client SDKs to send `x-idempotency-key`, consider a short warmup flow for the internal job (spread across 60s instead of firing all at once), and implement server-side dedupe for idempotent operations. Also consider adding a burst-budget service that tracks credits per tenant and allows controlled bursts without fully inflating refill rates.

infra-bot: created support ticket #12345 and attached runbook template.

maria: i'll apply the quick patch and monitor. i'll also ask the customer to add x-idempotency-key. thanks for the config snippets. i'll post metrics in this thread once we have 15m of post-change data.

customer-ops: thanks — on it. one last Q: if we enable hedging, how to limit scope?

sam: only enable hedging behind a feature flag on canary, restrict to read-only endpoints and per-tenant low-risk customers. use a short hedging window (e.g., 30-80ms) and make sure to dedupe at the backend. example: `hedge_ms: 50 jitter: 10ms`.

maria: noted. updating runbook now and will report back at 2398765489. :rocket:
